title: Design a Multi-Tenant Linear CI/CD Workflow Engine
prompt: Design a multi-tenant CI/CD service driven by Git webhooks and immutable YAML at a commit. Pipelines are linear: each job begins only after the previous job succeeds. Cover webhook idempotency, durable job state, fair sandbox scheduling, logs and artifacts, secrets, retries, deployment side effects, and tenant isolation.

response.placeholder: Pin configuration to a commit, then separate logical job completion from physical worker attempts.
response.reference_answer:
## Intake and state
Deduplicate Git deliveries, fetch the exact commit, validate the immutable linear configuration, and write a pipeline plus first logical job through an outbox. Logical states are durable; later jobs are created only after their predecessor succeeds.

## Execution
Schedule sandboxed jobs fairly by tenant under CPU, memory, image, and queue quotas. Workers receive attempt IDs, short-lived scoped credentials, isolated namespaces, restricted network policy, and immutable artifact locations. Stream logs with cursors and persist artifact digests.

## Failure semantics
Worker execution is at least once after a crash, not physically exactly once. Fence attempts and require deployment APIs to consume an idempotency key so the externally visible release is effectively once. Failure skips later logical jobs; retry creates a new attempt, not a duplicate state transition.

## Operations
Measure queue age, noisy-neighbor effects, cache hit rate, image-pull time, secret access failures, retry reasons, and deployment reconciliation.

## Progressive Hints
1. YAML without a commit hash is mutable configuration.
2. A job attempt is not the logical job.
3. Sandboxes are a tenancy boundary.
